content.intro: This lesson covers Choosing Between Box, Rc, Arc, and Interior-Mutability Types. It sits in Module 15, Smart Pointers and Interior Mutability, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Choosing Between Box, Rc, Arc, and Interior-Mutability Types matters when you work with unsafe invariants and external contracts. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Unsafe Rust permits a narrow set of operations whose safety obligations the compiler cannot fully prove. Every unsafe boundary needs explicit invariants, valid initialization, correct aliasing, and compatible external contracts.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Choosing Between Box, Rc, Arc, and Interior-Mutability Types, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Box provides single ownership of heap data, Rc shares ownership in one thread, Arc shares ownership across threads, and interior mutability changes when borrowing is checked.
